front: Sites of the four stages of aerobic respiration
back: Glycolysis: cytoplasm. Link reaction and Krebs cycle: matrix. Oxidative phosphorylation: inner membrane (cristae).
Phosphorylation (2 ATP) → fructose 1,6-bisphosphate → lysis to 2 triose phosphate → oxidation (2 reduced NAD) → 2 pyruvate (4 ATP made, net 2).
Pyruvate (3C) + CoA + NAD → acetyl CoA (2C) + CO₂ + reduced NAD.
Acetyl (2C) + oxaloacetate (4C) → citrate (6C) → 5C → 4C → oxaloacetate; 2 CO₂, 3 reduced NAD, 1 reduced FAD, 1 ATP per turn.

front: Products per glucose before oxidative phosphorylation
back: 6 CO₂, 10 reduced NAD, 2 reduced FAD, 4 ATP (net 2 from glycolysis, 2 from the Krebs cycle).
Removal of carbon dioxide from a molecule, by a decarboxylase.
Removal of hydrogen from a molecule (oxidation) by a dehydrogenase; NAD or FAD accepts it.

front: Why does the Krebs cycle need oxygen indirectly?
back: Oxygen is needed to re-oxidise reduced NAD and FAD at the electron transport chain; without it the dehydrogenations stop.
